key_insight: A continuously updated (live) benchmark reveals whether time-series forecasting models—especially foundation-style pretrained models—truly generalize across time, preventing test-set contamination and inflated evaluation scores.
problem_solved: Static train/test splits mask temporal distribution shifts and enable inadvertent use of test data (or test-driven model selection), giving overoptimistic evaluations of forecasting models.
method: Live benchmarking service that continuously rolls forward evaluation periods, keeping test data out of training and avoiding static-split leakage.
Controlled dataset curation, provenance tracking, and automated evaluation pipelines that recompute scores and leaderboards as new temporal slices arrive.
Auditable protocols for model submission and selection to ensure fair comparison across pretrained and task-specific models under realistic temporal shifts.
impact: Provides a realistic, contamination-resistant evaluation for time-series forecasting, enabling practitioners to trust model comparisons and choose models robust to temporal drift in production settings.
visual_elements: Timeline comparing static-split evaluation vs. Impermanent live rolling evaluation (showing contamination risk eliminated).
Pipeline diagram of data curation → provenance checks → live evaluation → leaderboard updates.
Heatmap or line chart showing model performance drift over successive evaluation windows (temporal generalization).
Icon set: clock (time/temporal), shield (contamination protection), leaderboard/trophy (fair comparison).
paper_title: Impermanent: A Live Benchmark for Temporal Generalization in Time Series Forecasting
paper_authors: Azul Garza, Renée Rosillo, Rodrigo Mendoza-Smith, David Salinas, Andrew Robert Williams
